title: Fallback Sandbox — operator journal and interaction sketches
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This doc is an operator-focused journal + working wireframe writeup for a "fallback sandbox" feature in the Rollouts console. The sandbox should let an operator rehearse automatic fallback policies, simulate traffic mixes, and evaluate canary/A-B behaviors without touching production routes. The goal is low-friction experimentation: surface failure modes, microcopy for operator decisions, and a short backlog of necessary UX polish items.

Audience / context:
- Primary: Console product PMs + engineers working on rollout policies and observability (Marco, Priya).
- Secondary: SREs and on-call engineers who will rely on fallbacks during incidents.
- Not final UX — this is intentionally rough, includes notes-to-self and open questions.

High-level concepts (operator mental model):
1) Sandbox runs in a simulated environment that uses live metrics and historical traces (opt-in) to replay traffic patterns.
2) Policy composer: create fallback policy candidates (route -> primary model, fallback model(s), region priorities, max-fallback-rate, cooldowns).
3) Rehearsal run: apply policy to replayed traffic and surface outcomes (latency distribution, error uplift, token-cost delta, user-visible drift).
4) Safety governor: automatically highlight policies that violate SLOs or exceed cost thresholds.
5) Promote: if results are acceptable, generate a deployment plan (canary config + rollout windows) or export policy as a JSON obj for infra pipeline.

Wireframe notes (interaction steps):
- Landing panel: "Create new sandbox rehearsal"
  - Quick inputs: target route (auto-complete), historical window (e.g., last 24h, last 7d), traffic slice (p50/p95/slow requests), sample size slider (10–100k requests), preserve user anonymity toggle.
  - Small help text: "Sandbox will replay metrics only — no change to live routing unless you promote the policy."

- Step 2: Policy builder (three-column composer)
  - Column A (Primary): select primary model/variant, traffic fraction that remains on primary (for partial fallback tests).
  - Column B (Fallbacks): add one or more fallback variants with priority and max-fallback-rate per minute. For each fallback row show estimated latency and cost delta badges (computed from model profiles).
  - Column C (Rules & constraints): conditions (latency > X ms, error rate > Y%, region-unavailable), cooldowns, and automatic rollback thresholds.
  - Microcopy example under rule: "If fallback activation triggers for >2% of requests over 1m, pause and notify on-call."

- Step 3: Rehearsal config and run
  - Buttons: "Run quick replay (fast, approximate)", "Run full replay (slower, deterministic)"
  - Live progress bar with estimated completion time and live metrics streaming (latency histograms, error rate, cost delta).
  - Highlight rows where SLOs are crossed in rehearsal with a red chevron and suggested fixes.

- Step 4: Results canvas (chart-first)
  - Multi-series timeline: primary vs fallback latency, 95th p99, error rate, token cost per 1k requests.
  - Heatmap: where fallbacks were invoked by route/region/client-id (sampled).
  - Side panel: "What changed" diff: comparative examples of model outputs on a few sampled prompts (displayed for engineers to eyeball regression).
  - Quick actions: "Adjust policy and rerun", "Export as rollout (canary config)", "Save as draft", "Create ticket (JIRA)".

Operator journal entries (real notes from a dry run):
- 2024-02-15: Ran a quick replay for /search-route. Found a case where fallback A increased cost by ~3.1x for long-context requests — need a model-profile adjustment to show cost per token for >1024 seq lengths.
- 2024-02-18: Observed that the rehearsal incorrectly counted cached responses as cold inference (false-positive latency spikes). Action: flag cache-hit awareness in replay engine (backlog item).
- 2024-02-22: Microcopy iteration — operators confused by "max-fallback-rate" label. Rename to "max fallback activations per minute" and add tooltip with example math.

Edge cases & safety checks to design for:
- Partial traffic & user sessions: when we simulate partial fallback (e.g., 10% of requests), we must ensure we map session continuity so developers understand possible user-visible regressions.
- Cross-region failover: rehearsal should be able to simulate a region outage; ensure routing priority semantics are tested.
- Observability blind spots: ensure KV cache/edge-caching isn't double-counted; surface a "data quality" tab if trace sampling was insufficient.
- Model variance: for A/B tests where the fallback is a different architecture, show sample prompts + output diff so product owners can approve or reject based on quality, not just metrics.

Open UX questions (for next iteration):
- How intrusive should suggested fixes be? E.g., auto-suggest lowering fallback rate vs. forcing manual confirm. Lean toward suggestions + one-click apply.
- Notifications model: should rehearsal results send ephemeral Slack messages or persist in the console timeline? Prefer both: ephemeral for ops, persisted for audit.
- Export format: JSON vs. Terraform vs. internal CD pipeline. MVP: JSON + JIRA auto-link.

Backlog (prioritized, short list):
1) Add cache-awareness flag to replay (HIGH) — JIRA-ROLL-412.
2) Rename max-fallback-rate + tooltip (MED) — quick copy change.
3) Add sample-output-diff diffs with side-by-side token-level highlights (HIGH).
4) Show model-profile costs broken out by seq-length buckets (MED).
5) Simulated region outage mode for rehearsal (LOW) — ability to toggle a region offline.
6) Add quick-promote flow that creates a canary with predefined safe defaults (MED) — ensure explicit confirmation.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Operator can author a fallback policy in the composer and run at least a "quick replay" using available historical traces.
- Rehearsal provides a results canvas that surfaces latency, error rate, and token-cost delta clearly and flags SLO violations.
- Operators can export the policy as a JSON snippet and create a JIRA ticket prefilled with the results summary.
- Sandbox runs are opt-in and do not change live routing unless the operator explicitly chooses "Promote to canary" and confirms.

Accessibility & microcopy considerations:
- All toggles need clear labels and example values (avoid percent-of-requests phrasing without examples).
- Use short, actionable microcopy for suggested fixes: e.g., "Reduce fallback rate to 2% and rerun rehearsal" rather than long paragraphs.

Follow-ups for engineering sync (short list of tasks for next meeting):
- Replay engine: add cache-awareness and a deterministic sample mode (owner: infra team, due: 2024-03-15).
- Model profile API: extend output to include per-sequence-length cost buckets (owner: serving-runtime, due: 2024-03-20).
- Console: prototype three-column composer layout with drag-to-reorder fallbacks (owner: DX, due: 2024-03-01).

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc intentionally mixes sketches, operator notes, and backlog items. Please comment inline with any risks we missed.
- Particularly interested in whether the suggested safety governor actions are too conservative or too permissive for enterprise SLA customers.

Unresolved questions (short):
- Should sandbox results be considered auditable for compliance? If yes, we need retention policies and exportable signed artifacts.
- Should the rehearsal environment be multi-tenant? For MVP keep it per-organization.

Quick copy snippet (for UI):
- Button: "Run rehearsal"
- Confirm dialog: "This will replay historical traffic for selected route. No live routing changes will occur. Promote to canary only after an explicit confirm."
- Tooltip for "cooldown": "Time window after a fallback activation during which another activation for the same rule will be suppressed."

---
End of operator journal snapshot.
(If you want a cleaned PRD or a printable wireframe doc, I can produce a separate final doc with images and tighter copy.)
